### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `090c5839486df9fa3d7f7f2b7a718fc6dc795fdd` — the merge of head `4bc8e16d39df2740f685b5aa0d82036ab7d2babb` into base `0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 090c5839486df9fa3d7f7f2b7a718fc6dc795fdd && git checkout 090c5839486df9fa3d7f7f2b7a718fc6dc795fdd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b 4bc8e16d39df2740f685b5aa0d82036ab7d2babb && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b && git merge --no-ff 4bc8e16d39df2740f685b5aa0d82036ab7d2babb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b0fe92782a38a43cc19bfd3ee97271a07cbf9f00`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts + packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/mail-hole-grammar.ts, packages/formula/src/template-formatter-shape.test.ts, packages/formula/src/template-unknown-formatter.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.formatter-shape.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.email-template-formatter-shape.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-formatter-shape.render.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/text-field-html-outlets.pin.test.ts (the floor: every non-prose path) + cited and read, not reviewed: packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/package.json (`exports`), packages/formula/src/mail-html-hole-placement.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, .changeset/26948-mail-unknown-formatter-formula.md, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md:444, ADR-0087 and `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`. Changesets, the two `content/docs/**` pages and the regenerated reference are not reviewed. Base: `main` at `1287b2fa`; head is 4 commits ahead, 9 behind (merge base `4d3a077f`); the diff read is GitHub's three-dot diff, which is the net diff against that base.

Ruling applied: claim `6469619404` on #27225 — the mail grammar accepts exactly the formatter parts the in-app compile accepts and refuses the rest; in-app is not narrowed.

### ① Derived judgments

Every judgment below is read off the code at the head and at the base, not off the PR body.

1. **Mail refuses a path followed by `|` whose formatter name is not one word — right.** `parseMailHole` no longer runs its own `FILTER_RE`; it splits the formatter part with `splitHoleFormatter` and hands the name to `judgeHoleFormatter`, whose new first branch after `one-formatter` returns `formatter-shape` when `!WORD_RE.test(formatter)`. A path + `|` therefore always parses, carrying the refusal, and every reader of `parseMailHole` / `judgeMailHoleGrammar` follows with no code change: the lint rule (`os validate`, `os build`, `os lint`), the runtime publish door (`422 INVALID_METADATA`, pinned in metadata-protocol) and the renderer (`render()` already throws `TEMPLATE_INVALID` on `parsed.refusal`; `email-service.ts` prefixes the template name and locale). Before, these holes were `null` and printed to the recipient verbatim. The published spec on `main` (`MAIL_TEMPLATE_HOLES`, the skill row at `SKILL.md:444`, the docs page) declares the shape `{{ path | formatter[:arg] }}` with a formatter the engine knows and never declared non-word formatter text as anything: this makes the spec's own refusal real.

2. **Mail now also judges a path + `|` whose name is a word but whose part the old `FILTER_RE` failed — right.** `{{ x | curency :EUR }}` reads `known-formatter` (as before, by a different route); `{{ amount | currency :currency_code }}` was printed verbatim at the base (`FILTER_RE` failed, the judge saw no argument) and now reads `currency-code-literal`. Both are the grammar's existing rules reaching holes they could not see.

3. **Mail widens to the in-app reading (the ruled-for parity) — right, one part undisclosed.** Parts the in-app dialect accepts and mail printed verbatim at the base now parse and render: a space before the colon (`currency :EUR`, `date :long`), an apostrophe in the argument (`default:it's`, `default:'it's'`, `default:n'a`), and `currency :@currency_code` (the `@path` form, `codePath` still resolved). One widening the PR and all three changesets deny: **`currency:"EUR"` (and `currency: "EUR"`) was REFUSED at the base** — `FILTER_RE` kept the double quotes in the argument, `isCurrencyCode('"EUR"')` is false and `currencyCodePath` found no `@`, so `currency-code-literal` fired at every authoring door and at render. At the head the quotes are stripped and the hole publishes and renders `€1,234.50`. That is the ruling's outcome (in-app accepted it before and after), so the behaviour is right; the formula changeset's sentence "No authoring door accepts anything it refused before" and the lint changeset's "No accept set is widened" are false for it. See S1.

4. **Mail reads every double-quoted argument without its quotes — right, disclosed as one instance where it is a class.** `splitHoleFormatter` strips one `'` or `"` at each end; `FILTER_RE` stripped only `'`. So every `name:"arg"` mail already rendered now renders differently, not only `default:"n/a"` → `n/a`: `date:"long"` (short style → long style), `truncate:"80"` (no cut, `Number('"80"')` was NaN → cut at 80), `number:"2"` / `percent:"1"` (unformatted → formatted), `default:""` (`""` → empty). Each is the in-app reading, so right under the ruling; the census (0 double-quoted arguments in any shipped template) covers the class. See S1.

5. **In-app behaviour is unchanged, byte for byte — proven from the moved code.** `splitHoleFormatter` is `parseHole`'s colon split verbatim: no colon → `{ name: part }` (so `arg` destructures to `undefined`, as the old `let arg` did); else `name = slice(0, colon).trim()`, `arg = slice(colon + 1).trim().replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '')`, the same two expressions. The judge's new `formatter-shape` branch fires for in-app too, but `parseHole` then falls through to the unchanged `if (!FORMATTERS[name]) return null`, and no key of `FORMATTERS` fails `\w+` (its own keys are the eleven formatter names; the inherited `Object.prototype` keys are all words), so for every non-word name `parseHole` returns `null` exactly as before and `compileTemplate` emits the same "invalid template hole … Known formatters" sentence. For a word name the condition `WORD_RE.test(f) && !TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS.includes(f)` became `!TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS.includes(f)` under a guard that is now always true: the same verdict. `evaluate()` re-parses with the same function. Pinned by the 19-part parity test (10 accepted, 9 refused, both dialects) and the in-app-sentence test.

6. **No mail spelling that rendered correctly at the base is refused at the head.** Enumerated from the two tokenizers: every part the old `FILTER_RE` matched has a `\w+` name, so `formatter-shape` cannot fire on it; `one-formatter` reads the unchanged `formatterPart`; the only argument that reads differently is the double-quoted class (item 4), which can only REMOVE a `currency-code-literal` refusal, never add one. The set of refused-at-the-head mail holes is the base's set plus items 1 and 2 only.

7. **Public surface — right.** `splitHoleFormatter` and `HoleFormatterParts` are exported from the module only; `packages/formula/src/index.ts` names its exports (no `export *`) and the package `exports` map has only `.`, so the package index exports nothing new, as the changeset says. `TemplateHoleGrammarRule` (a public type) gains `'formatter-shape'`: a widening of a union; the in-repo readers (lint, plugin-email, the placement judge) read `.rule` only to word a finding and no exhaustive switch exists. Disclosed in the changeset, as #26948 disclosed `'known-formatter'`.

8. **The placement judge changes with it — right, not named in the PR.** `judgeMailHtmlHoles` reads `parseMailHole`, so a path + `|` + non-word text is now a hole there too (and so for `validateEmailTemplateHolePlacements`). Benign: the grammar rule refuses the hole first, and the "same spans" pin still holds by construction because the corpus no longer carries a refused spelling and the new boundary case asserts the literal set is `[]` for the judge and verbatim for the renderer.

9. **Spec: describe() text and TSDoc only — right.** No schema accept set moves; `content/docs/references/system/email-template.mdx` is regenerated from it. `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`: `minor` with `!` and the `**BREAKING**` token, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — matches what each publishes (a mail accept-set narrowing visible at that package's own door: the grammar, the authoring rules, the render), at the level this repo gives a breaking change (no `major`, `check-changeset-no-major`), and matches the sibling #26948 entries on the same grammar. The PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line agrees with the changesets.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `patch`, `Clause-②: no` — right (item 9).
- ADR-0087: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` on the three narrowings. The gate's own detector admits it (no arrow rewrite, no framed FROM/TO table; "The remedy" is one sentence with one example hole). On the merits the D3 call holds: no key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; the refused text never formatted anything, so there is no old shape with a mapping for a conversion or a semantic step to carry; the refusal sentence at the door is the whole prescription; the census found 0 shipped templates. A semantic entry with `acceptanceCriteria` (the `flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused` shape) is the heavier form for a dialect-wide retirement with real usage; nothing here reaches that bar, and #26948 took the identical disposition on this grammar under its own contract review. Not required.
- The formula changeset says the #26948 entry is "superseded, in the same release" rather than correcting it: see S2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- **Dev note: the two dialects differ in the PATH part** (`PATH_ONLY_RE` admits `$` and `[i]`, mail `PATH_RE` does not). Answered: both grammars are declared — the mail spec says a hole's path is a dotted path of word characters, and the in-app `$` admission is #22110's — and both are enforced, so this is not a declared-rule-with-no-judge and no card is owed from this review. It is the exact edge of the :284 boundary (see ④) and would be its own card if anyone wants `{{ rows[0].x | upper }}` judged in mail.
- **Dev note: `default:"n/a"` reads differently.** Answered in ① items 3 and 4: it is the double-quoted-argument class plus the `currency:"EUR"` widening, to be disclosed as such (S1).
- **`dogfood_battery: NOT MEASURED`.** `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head completed `success` (its shards skipped by path filter); the full battery rides `main`'s push run after landing, and the serial order with #27249 forces a `main` merge on whichever lands second, so CI re-measures the final head either way. Not a blocker.
- **Merge order with #27249 (#26939).** This diff's only plugin-email source hunk is three header-comment lines and it does not touch `template-hole-grammar.test.ts`; the overlap is prose (the `IEmailService` TSDoc, `email-templates.mdx`, `template-engine.ts` of formula). Whichever lands second merges `main`; no stacking.
- **Check-runs on `b0fe9278` at the time of this record:** 33 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 0 failed, 6 still `in_progress` (`Test Core` 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`). Every completed gate is green, including `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Test Core` 1/8, 2/8, 7/8, 8/8, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`. The landing waits on the required nine finishing green as it always does; this record judges the contract and the narrowing, not the unfinished runs.
- Not a fork (head repo is the base repo); 590 changed lines; no governed-surface path in the file list.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing, against the published spec on `main`.** It takes no declared capability away at the consumer. The spec declared `{{ path | formatter[:arg] }}` with one formatter the engine knows; `date-long`, `two words` and an empty formatter part were never declared, were refused in-app, and in mail reached the recipient as formatter syntax only because `parseMailHole` returned `null` and the renderer's "not a hole" branch printed it. The refusal is placed in the shared judge, so the three doors and the renderer refuse the same hole with the same sentence through the one function they already read; nothing is narrowed at a consumer. The widening half is the ruling made mechanical: one tokenizer and one judge for both dialects, so parity cannot drift by construction, and the 19-part table pins it. The in-app dialect is not narrowed (① item 5).

**The boundary at `text-field-html-outlets.pin.test.ts:284` — right, and pinned on both sides.** The question "is this brace pair a hole" belongs to the path grammar (`PATH_RE`, unchanged by this card); "is this hole well formed" belongs to the formatter grammar (this card). Drawing the line at *a path followed by `|` is judged; brace text whose part before any `|` is not a path stays verbatim* means every brace pair that can be an author's formatter use is judged, while mail keeps its one legitimate verbatim case (a mail body may carry literal braces; the in-app engine refuses everything, having no such case). The residue — `{{ | upper }}`, `{{ a b | upper }}`, `{{ | date-long }}` — looks like a hole attempt but has no path, and it stays verbatim under the declared mail path grammar exactly as `{{ rows[0].x }}` does; moving it is a path-grammar decision, outside this card and named in ③. The new pin covers the literal set through the real renderer and the placement judge, and the refused set through both entry points, triple braces included, so the three readers agree by construction (one `parseMailHole`). The corpus edit (drop `{{ x | two words }}`, add `{{ a b | upper }}`) keeps the "same spans" case honest. Accepted.

**Tried to break it.** (a) A non-word key on `FORMATTERS` that would make `parseHole` return a hole where it returned `null` — none exists (① item 5). (b) A mail spelling accepted at the base and refused at the head — none (① item 6). (c) `currency :@currency_code` with the space — `currencyCodePath` reads the trimmed name before the colon, so the `@path` form survives the new tokenizer; tested. (d) A `|` inside a quoted argument (`default:'a | b'`) — `chainsASecondFormatter` reads the unchanged `formatterPart`; unchanged. (e) `{{ x | :EUR }}` — name is empty, the sentence says "writes no formatter name after the `|`"; acceptable for an author who wrote `:EUR`. (f) ReDoS — `splitHoleFormatter`'s one regex is two anchored single-character alternatives; `WORD_RE` is `^\w+$`; linear. (g) The placement judge now listing refused holes — benign (① item 8). No must-fix.

**Should-fix.**

- **S1 (changesets and PR body: disclose the class, and the one widening).** State that a formatter part the in-app dialect accepts now publishes and renders in mail even where mail refused it before — `currency:"EUR"` was refused by `currency-code-literal` at every door and at render, and now publishes — and that *every* double-quoted argument loses its quotes (`date:"long"`, `truncate:"80"`, `number:"2"`, `default:""`), not only `default:"n/a"`. Replace "No authoring door accepts anything it refused before" (formula) and "No accept set is widened" (lint) with the true sentence: the mail accept set widens to the in-app reading of the formatter part, per the ruling, and narrows by the non-word names. The level does not move (a widening under `minor` with the narrowing already declared), which is why this is not a must-fix; but the changeset is the release's input and a false accept-set sentence ships verbatim into the CHANGELOG, where only a dedicated docs PR can amend it later.
- **S2 (correct the unreleased #26948 sentence in place).** `.changeset/26948-mail-unknown-formatter-formula.md` still says text after the `|` that is not a single word "still names no formatter and is left as written". It is unreleased and ships in the same release as this entry; edit that sentence in that file (one line) instead of carrying a "Supersedes, in the same release" paragraph, so the compiled CHANGELOG never states a behaviour that was false on the day it was published.
- **S3 (one stale docs line on the page this PR edits).** `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx:155`, "An unknown formatter falls back to the raw value rather than failing the render.", has been false since #27217 and now contradicts three rules on the same page, one of them added by this PR above it. Delete the line in this PR; the page is already in the diff.

Non-blocking observation: the header of `mail-hole-grammar.ts` says the two dialects "refuse the rest with the same sentence"; for `formatter-shape` and `known-formatter` the in-app dialect keeps its own sentence by design (pinned). "the same verdict" would be exact. Comment only.
